name: Dia African rice evidence
description: Rice grains at Dia, Mali, provide evidence for a West African rice food system during the first millennium BCE.

date.label: Three individual calibrated ranges between 799 and 411 BCE
date.basis: Date applies to the scoped observation or event; it is not a claim of global origin.

events.statement: Rice grains at Dia, Mali, provide evidence for a West African rice food system during the first millennium BCE.

evidence.supports: Three early rice samples from Dia have calibrated intervals of 799–413, 785–411 and 791–413 BCE. Most rice remains lacked diagnostic husks, so the domestic status of each early grain is not established; the broader assemblage is interpreted as consistent with African rice cultivation.

events.caveats: The three dated grains have different intervals. Most remains lacked diagnostic husks; the domestic status of the early specimens is uncertain. Broader assemblage comparisons suggest African rice cultivation but do not prove the origin or independently identify each early grain.
